review_notes: I read the whole file and grepped Mathlib for uses of the pseudoelement API. Only this file and Counterexamples/Pseudoelement.lean use it. I could not run Lean, so I have not tested whether the proposed attributes cause any simp confluence problems. The existing simp set (`app_hom`, `zero_eq_zero`, `apply_zero`, `zero_apply`) looks coherent. Both findings are about missing simp coverage of the function-on-pseudoelements interface.

findings.excerpt: theorem pseudoApply_mk' {P Q : C} (f : P ⟶ Q) (a : Over P) : f ⟦a⟧ = ⟦↑(a.hom ≫ f)⟧ := rfl
findings.problem: This is the basic evaluation rule for `f` on a class `⟦a⟧`, but it is not a simp lemma. The file's proofs use it only by naming it each time: `rw [pseudoZero_def, pseudoApply_mk']` in `apply_zero` and `zero_apply`, and `simp [over_coe_def, pseudoApply_mk', h]` in `apply_eq_zero_of_comp_eq_zero`. Without it, simp cannot reduce `f ⟦a⟧` to a class of an arrow. It also lacks the other simp lemmas that would then fire, such as `Over.coe_hom` and `zero_eq_zero`. The name uses a prime (it is listed in `nolints_prime_decls`), which hides that it is the canonical unfolding lemma.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `pseudoApply_mk'` as `@[simp]`, and consider `over_coe_def` in the same way. The unfolding is one-directional and terminating: the left side contains `pseudoApply`, and the right side is a `Quotient.mk` of a composite arrow. Then `apply_eq_zero_of_comp_eq_zero` could be `by simp [h]`, and the `rw [pseudoZero_def, pseudoApply_mk']; simp` steps could be simplified. If `Quot.mk`-versus-`⟦⟧` forms cause trouble, state the rule with the form that simp produces. Keep `pseudoZero_def` non-simp so that `0` is not unfolded.
findings.benefit: Chasing proofs that use `simp` get the standard normal form for `f ⟦a⟧` without each call listing `pseudoApply_mk'`. The three existing proofs shrink and become less fragile.

evidence.excerpt: fun h => by simp [over_coe_def, pseudoApply_mk', h]

findings.excerpt: theorem comp_apply {P Q R : C} (f : P ⟶ Q) (g : Q ⟶ R) (a : P) : (f ≫ g) a = g (f a) :=
findings.problem: `comp_apply` is the canonical functoriality rule: it splits a composite morphism applied to a pseudoelement into iterated application. It is not tagged `@[simp]`, although `apply_zero` and `zero_apply` are. As a result, `simp` can prove `f 0 = 0` but cannot simplify `(f ≫ g) a`. `comp_comp` is the same fact in the opposite direction (`g ∘ f = f ≫ g`), and the file never states which form is normal. The `comp_apply` docstring says the identity is not definitional, so `rfl`-based reductions cannot replace it.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp]` to `comp_apply`, so that `(f ≫ g) a` normalizes to `g (f a)`. This orientation terminates because it strictly removes a `≫` from the argument of the coercion. It is also compatible with `apply_zero` and `zero_apply`, which then apply to the inner or outer application. Keep `comp_comp` non-simp so the two do not compete.
findings.benefit: Diagram chases, which this file exists to support, would reduce compositions of morphisms on pseudoelements automatically. Users would get one normal form (iterated application) and would not need to cite `comp_apply` by hand.

evidence.excerpt: theorem zero_apply {P : C} (Q : C) (a : P) : (0 : P ⟶ Q) a = 0 :=
